Supported standard (2026-10-27): a claim about code passes only if the notes state it, in prose or in a code comment; it fails if it has to be worked out by reading or running the code. Returning -1 when the target isn't found appears only as `return -1` in the code.
No-leakage standard (2026-10-27): a card fails if a code snippet, formula or name in the question spells out the answer. The name NADPH in the question spells out the answer, NADP+.

Atomic standard (2026-10-27): a card fails if it splits naturally into separate questions; a closed set passes only when the notes say the same thing about each item and the list is complete. Real GDP adjusting for price changes and nominal GDP not adjusting are separate facts that split naturally into two questions.

Atomic standard (2026-10-27): a card fails if it splits naturally into separate questions; a closed set passes only when the notes say the same thing about each item and the list is complete. Comparing the target with the middle element and discarding half of the remaining interval split naturally into two questions.
